title: The Evening Brief: Markets drift lower as whale flows shift onto exchanges
dek: Monday brought a broad pullback across major cryptocurrencies with little fresh news to drive the session. The day's signal came from exchange flows: $1.6 billion in combined assets moved onto exchanges over the week, led by $1.2 billion in bitcoin, a reversal from last week's modest accumulation pattern.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
key_fact: Whale accumulation reversed this week as $1.6 billion moved onto exchanges, with bitcoin seeing the largest inflow and ETF investors turning net sellers on October 23, signaling a shift in conviction despite technical structures that remain long-biased.
bottom_line: Monday saw modest price declines across the board with no fresh news catalysts, the day driven instead by a reversal in whale flow patterns: $1.6 billion moved onto exchanges over the week ending October 26, led by bitcoin, after the prior week saw accumulation off-venue. Spot Bitcoin ETF flows split the week, outflows on October 23 against cumulative inflows, signaling mixed conviction. Leverage remains long-heavy across major venues, and technicals show mild oversold conditions with golden crosses intact but momentum below signal lines; the reporting does not say whether Monday's flows reflect profit-taking or repositioning ahead of coming regulatory dates. Watch for the CLARITY Act checkpoint on January 1, 2027, and Russia's regulatory milestone on December 1, 2026, both live in the desk's regulatory watch.
body: Monday's market action was quiet on news and driven by technicals and flows. Bitcoin down 0.70% over 24 hours, Ether down 1.32% over 24 hours, and Solana down 1.43% over 24 hours, with losses broadening to altcoins: Dogecoin down 0.12% over 24 hours, XRP down 0.85% over 24 hours, and Cardano down 0.20% over 24 hours. Over longer windows the pressure deepened: Bitcoin down 2.40% over seven days and down 4.79% over thirty days; Ether down 3.36% over seven days and down 13.53% over thirty days; Solana down 2.65% over seven days and down 17.07% over thirty days. BNB held steadier, little changed over 24 hours but up 2.07% over seven days, even as it remained down 5.06% over thirty days.

The week-to-date pattern reflects late-week selling pressure that offset earlier accumulation. Separately, the desk's Whale Watch board tracked broader exchange flows over the week ending October 26. A total of $1.6 billion in combined assets moved onto exchanges, with bitcoin accounting for $1.2 billion and Ether for $373 million. This reverses last week's pattern: the week ending October 19 saw $205 million move off exchanges, while the weeks ending October 5 and October 12 had seen $365 million and $1.4 billion move onto exchanges respectively.

On leverage, funding rates on OKX held steady with Bitcoin and Ether both at 0.01% over 8 hours (11.0% annualized), suggesting balanced positioning despite the inflows onto venues. Long-to-short ratios remained skewed, with Bitcoin at 2.22:1 on OKX, Ether at 2.68:1, and Solana at 3.12:1, indicating longs remain crowded relative to shorts. Liquidations over recent windows showed mostly long-side pain: Bitcoin saw $659,737 in long liquidations versus $161,661 in shorts over a 7-hour window; Ether saw $549,521 in long liquidations and zero shorts over a 4-hour window; Solana saw $1.3 million in longs liquidated against $440 in shorts over 7 hours. Fear and Greed held at 50 (Neutral), at the midpoint of its 30-day range of 50 to 74, indicating no extreme positioning.

Technically, per the desk's boards, Bitcoin remains above its 200-day moving average and below its 12-month high by 36.1%, while a golden cross (50 crossing above 200-day SMA) is in place. RSI14 at 40.6 sits in mild oversold territory, as does Ether at 32.5 and Solana at 34.0, all with MACD below signal lines. The structure suggests neither exhaustion nor conviction. Among movers, XDC up 7.48% over 24 hours, NIGHT up 7.38% over 24 hours, and QNT up 4.89% over 24 hours led gainers, while ZRO down 8.04% over 24 hours, LIT down 5.91% over 24 hours, and GRAM down 4.22% over 24 hours led losers. The total crypto market cap stands at $2.68 trillion, with Bitcoin dominance at 59.5%.
